title: What can science teach us about the benefits of religion? With David DeSteno, PhD

sentences.en: For thousands of years, people have turned to religion to answer questions about how to lead a happy, moral, and fulfilling life,
sentences.zh: 几千年来，人们一直求助于宗教，以寻求如何过上幸福、道德和充实的生活，

sentences.en: how to meet life's challenges, and how to be resilient in the face of hardship.
sentences.zh: 如何应对生活的挑战，以及如何在逆境中保持韧性等问题的答案。

sentences.en: And for many people, religion's answers have proven satisfying.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，宗教提供的答案已被证明是令人满意的。

sentences.en: A 2019 Pew Research poll found that people who described themselves as actively religious, those who were affiliated with a religion and attended religious services regularly,
sentences.zh: 皮尤研究中心2019年的一项民意调查发现，那些自认为是积极的宗教信徒，即那些有宗教信仰并定期参加宗教仪式的人，

sentences.en: were more likely to say that they were very happy than people who didn't go to services or who were unaffiliated with any organized religion.
sentences.zh: 比那些不参加仪式或没有任何组织化宗教信仰的人，更有可能表示自己非常幸福。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: How do the structures and traditions of religion contribute to people's health, happiness, and well-being?
sentences.zh: 宗教的结构和传统是如何促进人们的健康、幸福和福祉的？

sentences.en: What can behavioral scientists learn from studying the religious rituals that scaffold people's lives from birth to coming of age to marriage to death?
sentences.zh: 行为科学家能从研究那些贯穿人们从出生、成年礼、结婚到死亡等人生阶段的宗教仪式中学到什么？

sentences.en: And can those lessons be applied outside the context of religious belief?
sentences.zh: 这些经验教训能否应用在宗教信仰之外的语境中？

sentences.en: What about the perennial question that pits science against religion?
sentences.zh: 那么那个让科学与宗教对立的永恒问题又该如何看待呢？

sentences.en: Can one be a scientist and still believe in a higher power?
sentences.zh: 一个人既是科学家，又能相信有超自然力量存在吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. David Desteno, a professor of psychology at Northeastern University in Boston, where he directs the Social Emotions Lab.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是波士顿东北大学的心理学教授大卫·德斯泰诺博士，他在那里负责社会情感实验室。

sentences.en: Dr. Desteno studies the ways in which people's emotions influence their social behavior and moral decision-making
sentences.zh: 德斯泰诺博士研究人们的情感如何影响其社会行为和道德决策，

sentences.en: in areas including trust, altruism, cooperation, resilience, dishonesty, and prejudice.
sentences.zh: 研究领域包括信任、利他主义、合作、韧性、不诚实和偏见等。

sentences.en: In recent years, he's been particularly interested in what behavioral science can learn from religious traditions
sentences.zh: 近年来，他特别感兴趣的是行为科学能从宗教传统中学到什么，

sentences.en: about how to help people improve their well-being and lead happier lives.
sentences.zh: 以帮助人们改善福祉并过上更幸福的生活。

sentences.en: He explores this topic in his book, How God Works, The Science Behind the Benefits of Religion,
sentences.zh: 他在九月份出版的著作《上帝如何运作：宗教益处背后的科学》以及同名播客中探讨了这一主题，该播客也于九月首播。

sentences.en: published in September, and in a podcast by the same name, which debuted in September.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，德斯泰诺博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us, Dr. Desteno.
sentences.zh: 你好，金。

sentences.en: Hi, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me on.
sentences.zh: 许多关于科学与宗教的讨论都将其框定为冲突，认为这是两种看待世界的对立方式。

sentences.en: Many discussions of science and religion are framed in terms of conflict, that these are two opposing ways of looking at the world.
sentences.zh: 但在你的书中，你认为科学家，特别是行为科学家，可以从研究宗教中学到很多东西。

sentences.en: But in your book, you argue that scientists can learn a great deal from studying religion, particularly behavioral scientists.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从这里开始吧。

sentences.en: So let's start with them.
sentences.zh: 作为一名研究心理学家，是什么激发了你对宗教的兴趣，并让你决定这值得研究？

sentences.en: As a research psychologist, what sparked your interest in religion and made you decide that it was something you needed to study?
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢你的提问。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you for that question.
sentences.zh: 我想明确一点，我在这方面并没有预设议程。

sentences.en: I want to be clear that I didn't have an agenda in this.
sentences.zh: 我开始这项工作并不是为了证明宗教对人们是有益还是有害的。

sentences.en: I didn't start out on this line of work to prove religion was beneficial or harmful to people.
sentences.zh: 我只是像任何优秀的科学家一样，遵循数据。

sentences.en: I just simply follow the data like any good scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 在我的实验室里，我们长期研究人们如何变得更友善、更有同情心，如何建立联系，以及如何变得更有韧性。

sentences.en: And for a long time in my lab, you know, we study things like how people become more kind and compassionate, how they form connection, how they become more resilient.
sentences.zh: 每当我们发现某种新的机制、策略或生活窍门来帮助实现这些目标时，

sentences.en: And every time we would find some new mechanism or some new strategy or life hack to help this,
sentences.zh: 我环顾四周，总会发现它们被用于各种宗教仪式中。

sentences.en: I'd look around and see it being used in all types of religious rituals.
sentences.zh: 我最终有一位学生对冥想本身及其最初的神学目的非常感兴趣，

sentences.en: And I finally had one student who was very much interested in meditation itself and what its original theological purpose was,
sentences.zh: 据佛教徒所说，冥想的目的不是为了提高记忆力，也不是为了提高标准化考试成绩，而是为了减少所有众生的痛苦。

sentences.en: according to the Buddhists, which is not to improve your memory, not to raise your standardized test scores, but to reduce the suffering of all sentient beings.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们进行了一些研究，实际上证明了在经过八周的冥想后，人们会变得更加自发地友善。

sentences.en: And so we ran some studies where we actually showed that after eight weeks of meditation, people became more spontaneously kind.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们雇佣演员，让他们看起来处于痛苦中并需要帮助。

sentences.en: That is, we would use actors and have them looking like they were in pain and needing help.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，与随机对照组相比，那些参与冥想的人，

sentences.en: And we would find people who were engaged in meditation compared to randomized controls
sentences.zh: 会突然变得更愿意帮助他们。

sentences.en: would suddenly become more willing to help them.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始意识到，我们所做的许多工作，我们所研究的许多机制，早在很久很久以前就被宗教思想家直觉地发现了。

sentences.en: And so what I began to realize is a lot of the work we were doing, a lot of the mechanisms we were studying have been intuited by religious thinkers long, long ago.
sentences.zh: 对于科学家来说，这很令人谦卑，对吧？

sentences.en: For scientists, that's humbling, right?
sentences.zh: 当有人提出你的想法时，这已经足够令人谦卑了。

sentences.en: It's always when someone, when someone has your idea, that's humbling enough.
sentences.zh: 但当他们比你早几千年就做到了这一点时，那真是非常令人谦卑。

sentences.en: But when they beat you to it by thousands of years, it's really, it's really humbling.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我不认为我们能从宗教中学到多少关于宇宙本质或疾病生物学的知识。

sentences.en: And, you know, I don't think we're going to learn much about the nature of the cosmos or the biology of disease from religion.
sentences.zh: 但如果几千年来旨在帮助人们应对生活挑战的思想毫无价值，那才奇怪呢。

sentences.en: But it would be strange if thousands of years of thought meant to help people meet the challenges of life didn't have something to offer.
sentences.zh: 所以我用的类比是，你知道，有时当制药公司寻找药物来帮助人们时，他们会求助于传统文化。

sentences.en: And so the analogy I use is, you know, sometimes when pharmaceutical companies are looking for medications to help people, they will look to traditional cultures.
sentences.zh: 当然，传统文化使用的许多药物可能无效，但有些确实有效。

sentences.en: And sure, a lot of those medications that traditional cultures use might not help, but some do.
sentences.zh: 我们通过这些研究发现了治疗各种癌症和其他疾病的绝佳药物。

sentences.en: And we found wonderful medications to treat different types of cancer and other ailments from those examinations.
sentences.zh: 我认为在心理学和人类福祉方面，我们也应该这样做。

sentences.en: I think we should do the same when it comes to psychology and human well-being.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在冥想方面已经做了一些尝试。

sentences.en: You know, we've done that a little bit with meditation.

sentences.en: We know it reduces stress and anxiety, but mindfulness can't be the only spiritual technique that has something to offer.
sentences.zh: 所以我的观点是，让我们把各种主义放在一边。

sentences.en: And so my argument here is, let's put our isms aside.

sentences.zh: 任何称职的科学家都会告诉你，他们可能看不到证据，但他们无法最终证明上帝不存在。

sentences.en: Any scientist worth their salt will tell you, you know, they may see no evidence of it, but they can't prove with finality that God doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不要争论这个问题。

sentences.en: So let's not argue about that.
sentences.zh: 让我们尊重每个人的观点，把这些放在一边，专注于我们能关注的事情，即这些实践如何让人们的生活变得更好。

sentences.en: Let's respect everybody's views, put those to the side and focus on what we can focus on, which is how these practices make life better for people.
sentences.zh: 我们能从中汲取什么知识和智慧？

sentences.zh: 很难根据一组特定的行为来定义仪式，因为有时这些行为是仪式的一部分，有时则不是。

sentences.en: I mean, what's the difference between lighting a candle so I can see my food better versus lighting a candle for Shabbat or for some other religious purpose?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你做的是同样的动作。

sentences.en: You know, you're doing the same action.
sentences.zh: 所以，目前最好的定义是，仪式是带有特殊意图的行为。

sentences.en: And so really, the best definition out there is that rituals are actions that are done with the special intention.

sentences.en: Well, there's work from my lab and others that shows when people do things in unison, even if they simply move their arms in time in unison with each other, it makes them feel more

sentences.zh: 在“坐七日丧”期间，家里的镜子会被遮住。

sentences.en: And so it makes sure that the community does this and repeatedly for a period of days.
sentences.zh: 这看起来可能有点奇怪，而且有神学上的原因。

sentences.en: Mirrors are covered in a household during shiva.
sentences.zh: 但也有心理学研究表明，当你照镜子时，你所感受到的任何情绪都会被放大。

sentences.en: It might seem kind of strange and there's a theological reason for it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你感到快乐，你会变得更快乐。

sentences.en: But there's also psychological research that shows when you look into a mirror, whatever emotion you are feeling becomes amplified.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到悲伤，你会变得更悲伤。

sentences.en: So if you're feeling happy, you get happier.
sentences.zh: 或者在悲伤的时候，那意味着更多的悲伤。

sentences.en: If you're feeling sad, you become sad.
sentences.zh: 所以通过遮住镜子，你所做的是稍微减轻了悲伤。

sentences.en: Or at a time of grief, that would mean more grief.
sentences.zh: 你坐在低处，或者坐在矮椅子上，或者坐在地上。

sentences.en: So by covering the mirrors, what you're doing is reducing grief a bit.
sentences.zh: 有新的神经科学研究表明，嗯，如果你坐在低处，从人体工程学上讲，那会开始导致你的下背部和膝盖不适。

sentences.en: You sit low to the ground or on low chairs or on the ground.
sentences.zh: 然后当你站起来迎接人们时，这种不适就消失了。

sentences.en: There's new neuroscience research that shows, well, if you sit low to the ground, ergonomically, that's going to start to cause discomfort in your lower back and knees.
sentences.zh: 有新的神经科学研究表明，当你出现这种轻微的不适感时，它会减少反刍和悲伤。

sentences.en: And then when you get up to welcome people, it goes away.
sentences.zh: 人们聚集在一起，以10人一组，称为“米尼扬”，10人或更多，一起祈祷并吟诵，一起背诵。

sentences.en: There's new neuroscience research that shows when you have mild onsets and offsets of discomfort like that, it reduces rumination and grief.
sentences.zh: 同样，你看到了那种同步性。

sentences.en: People come together and in groups of 10 called dominion, 10 or more, to say prayers together and chant them, to recite them together.
sentences.zh: 我们有实验证据表明，这种同步性增加了同情心和互相帮助的意愿。

sentences.en: Again, there you see that synchrony happening.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是一个例子，但你可以看到，这些不是随机的元素。

sentences.en: Synchrony that we know we have experimental evidence that increases feelings of compassion and willing to help each other.
sentences.zh: 它们通过岁月，找到了某些对身心的暗示，帮助我们应对我们面临的任何挑战。

sentences.en: And so this is just one example, but what you can see is these aren't random elements.
sentences.zh: 所以你写到非宗教人士如何能从世俗仪式中获得心理益处。

sentences.en: They, through the ages, have figured out certain nudges to the mind and the body that help us deal with whatever challenge we're facing.
sentences.zh: 如果有人，比如说，加入合唱团或管弦乐队，或者加入垒球队，甚至成为共济会成员，效果是一样的吗？

sentences.en: So you write about how people who are not religious can derive psychological benefits from secular rituals.
sentences.zh: 是否有与本质上一起表演所获得的心理和生理益处相似的益处？

sentences.en: Are the effects the same if someone, say, joins a chorus or an orchestra or joins a softball team or even becomes a mason, for example?
sentences.zh: 这就是你刚才谈到的。

sentences.en: Are there psychological and physiological benefits that are similar to those that are derived from essentially performing together?
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这有两部分。

sentences.en: That's what you were just talking about.
sentences.zh: 一是，你知道，人们经常说，嗯，这些不是宗教的好处吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so there are two parts to that.
sentences.zh: 为了清楚起见，你知道，除了你提到的皮尤的研究外，还有来自

sentences.en: One is, you know, people often say, well, aren't these benefits of religion?
sentences.zh: 梅奥诊所的研究和哈佛人类繁荣中心项目的研究表明，

sentences.en: And just to be clear, you know, besides the work you mentioned from Pew, there's research
sentences.zh: 那些参与信仰活动的人，不仅仅是说我相信，而是实际上

sentences.en: from the Mayo Clinic and research from the Harvard Center for Human Flourishing program showing
sentences.zh: 定期参与信仰活动，预示着更低的死亡率、更好的心血管健康、更好的心理健康，以及所有这类事情。

sentences.en: that people who engage in the activities of their faith, not just saying I believe, but actually
sentences.zh: 所以作为一名科学家，这告诉我他们所做的事情很重要。

sentences.en: engaging regularly in the activities of their faith, predicts lower mortality, better cardiovascular health, better mental health, all types of things like that.
sentences.zh: 正如你所建议的那样，人们经常说的一件事是，这不就是聚在一起吗？

sentences.en: And so as a scientist, what that tells me is something that they're doing matters.
sentences.zh: 当然，社区对人类的福祉来说是一个重要的部分。

sentences.en: And one thing that people often say, as you suggested, well, isn't it just coming together?
sentences.zh: 但仅仅聚在一起是不够的，你还需要有某种结构化的方式来利用这些机制，就像宗教仪式所做的那样。

sentences.en: And sure, community is an important part of well-being for humans.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么世俗仪式如果设计得当，也能产生类似的效果。

sentences.en: Being lonely is terrible for our mental and physical well-being.
sentences.zh: 孤独对我们的身心健康都有极大的危害。

sentences.en: But the data suggests that the benefits are more than just what you get from joining into any club.
sentences.zh: 但数据表明，其益处不仅仅来自于加入某个俱乐部。

sentences.en: And I think that's because in these faith traditions, there are these other practices that bring people together.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为在这些信仰传统中，存在着其他能将人们凝聚在一起的实践活动。

sentences.en: And we can talk, you know, more about them.
sentences.zh: 我们可以多聊聊这些内容。

sentences.en: But that example of rituals I just said, that not only bring people together, but build that sense of community and belief.
sentences.zh: 但我刚才提到的仪式示例，不仅能将人们聚在一起，还能建立起一种社区感和信仰感。

sentences.en: And so, yes, if you engage in actions like synchrony, like I was saying, so rather than saying
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，如果你参与像我刚才说的同步动作，而不是一起

sentences.en: prayers together or chanting together, do other motions together, that will make you feel closer to one another.
sentences.zh: 祈祷或吟唱，而是共同做其他动作，这会让你感到彼此更加亲近。

sentences.en: We have data in my lab to show that.
sentences.zh: 我的实验室有数据可以证明这一点。

sentences.en: But the data also suggests that when you add on these other elements of belief, et cetera, that the effects are stronger.
sentences.zh: 但数据也表明，当你加入信仰等其他要素时，效果会更强。

sentences.en: So, we don't really know how much stronger overall.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们并不真正知道整体上强了多少。

sentences.en: So, the best that I can say right now is if you do these rituals in a very secular way, you will get benefits from them.
sentences.zh: 因此，我现在能说的最好结论是，如果你以非常世俗的方式进行这些仪式，你也能从中获益。

sentences.en: Is the benefit exactly equivalent to what you would get if you have on, if you add on the multi-layered aspects of belief?
sentences.zh: 这种益处是否等同于你加入多层面的信仰要素后所能获得的呢？

sentences.en: We don't know that for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们还不能确定。

sentences.en: So, not to be flippant, but is there a difference if I'm, say, in a chorus singing the Verdi Requiem versus singing the Sound of Music?
sentences.zh: 所以，并不是想轻率地回答，但如果我是在合唱团唱威尔第的《安魂曲》，还是唱《音乐之声》，会有区别吗？

sentences.en: You know, would I be getting different benefits?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我获得的益处会不同吗？

sentences.en: Because it's non-secular music.
sentences.zh: 因为那是世俗音乐。

sentences.en: In that case, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我认为不会。

sentences.en: But there are certain rituals where the belief element is strongly important.
sentences.zh: 但有些仪式中，信仰要素是非常重要的。

sentences.en: So, for example, one area is if we look at healing rituals, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我们看看疗愈仪式，对吧？

sentences.en: We know that the placebo effect is very powerful.
sentences.zh: 我们知道安慰剂效应非常强大。

sentences.en: In fact, it accounts for about 30% of therapeutic effect of any medication.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它占了任何药物治疗效果的约30%。

sentences.en: And, you know, people hear the idea of the placebo effect, they think of that as kind of a derogatory thing or a derisive thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，人们听到安慰剂效应这个概念时，会觉得这是一种贬义或嘲讽的东西。

sentences.en: But it's actually not.
sentences.zh: 但实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: It's the evidence of the body to heal itself.
sentences.zh: 这是身体自我疗愈能力的证据。

sentences.en: And physicians have been using this forever.
sentences.zh: 医生们一直都在利用这一点。

sentences.en: And so, there's wonderful evidence suggesting that belief in something and its ability to heal you can actually account for a good deal of the healing that goes on.
sentences.zh: 因此，有极好的证据表明，对某事物的信念及其治愈你的能力，实际上可以解释很大一部分发生的疗愈过程。

sentences.en: In fact, there's something amazing that even called open-label placebos, which are placebos work for you even when you know they're placebos, if you believe in the placebo effect.
sentences.zh: 事实上，还有一种令人惊奇的东西叫“开放标签安慰剂”，即使你知道那是安慰剂，只要你相信安慰剂效应，它依然对你有效。

sentences.en: And so, I think what belief really does from a psychological standpoint is it sets your mind's expectations and predictions about what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为从心理学角度来看，信念真正起到的作用是设定了你大脑对即将发生之事的期望和预测。

sentences.en: Whether you ascribe that happening to the influence of a divine being or whether you ascribe that
sentences.zh: 无论你将这种发生归因于神灵的影响，还是归因于

sentences.en: happening to the belief of the power of something else doesn't matter in the sense of how it's going to affect your body.
sentences.zh: 对某种事物力量的信念，就它如何影响你的身体而言，这并不重要。

sentences.en: But I think that element of belief is where you can get a stronger benefit than just the actions of the breathing or singing on its own.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，正是这种信念要素，能让你获得比单纯的呼吸或唱歌动作本身更强的益处。

sentences.en: So, a few moments ago, you were talking a little bit about meditation, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，刚才你谈到了一点关于冥想的内容，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a religious practice that's been studied by scientists, but it's also moved into the secular world as well.
sentences.zh: 这是一种已被科学家研究过的宗教实践，但也已经进入了世俗世界。

sentences.en: How do the scientific findings about meditation fit into the traditional religious understanding of the purpose of meditation?
sentences.zh: 关于冥想的科学发现，是如何与传统宗教对冥想目的的理解相契合的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, meditation has been being studied scientifically for, you know, a decade or two now.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，冥想在科学上已经被研究了大概一二十年了。

sentences.en: And a lot of that actually happened because the Dalai Lama himself is very open to scientific study of it and actually funded a lot of research.
sentences.zh: 而且很多研究之所以能实现，是因为达赖喇嘛本人对科学研究非常开放，并资助了大量研究。

sentences.en: But initially, it was picked up by cognitive neuroscientists who were interested in what does it do to your brain?
sentences.zh: 但最初，它是由认知神经科学家们关注的，他们感兴趣的是它对你的大脑有什么影响？

sentences.en: And so, you know, we found out wonderful things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们发现了奇妙的事情。

sentences.en: Meditation actually alters the physical structure of your brain.
sentences.zh: 冥想实际上改变了你大脑的物理结构。

sentences.en: It increases your memory.
sentences.zh: 它增强了你的记忆力。

sentences.en: It increases your ability to have attention, focus your attention.
sentences.zh: 它增强了你的专注能力，即集中注意力的能力。

sentences.en: It reduces stress.
sentences.zh: 它能减轻压力。

sentences.en: But if you talk to the monks like I have and the Buddhist lamas, what they'll tell you is, yes, it will reduce your stress.
sentences.zh: 但如果你像我一样去和僧侣以及佛教喇嘛交谈，他们会告诉你，是的，它确实能减轻压力。

sentences.en: Yes, it will increase your memory.
sentences.zh: 是的，它确实能增强记忆力。

sentences.en: But that is not its purpose, right?
sentences.zh: 但那并不是它的目的，对吧？

sentences.en: Those things happen along the way.
sentences.zh: 那些只是过程中的副产品。

sentences.en: Its purpose is as a tool to reduce the suffering of all sentient beings.
sentences.zh: 它的目的是作为一种工具，来减少所有众生的痛苦。

sentences.en: That is, yourself, through meditation, you suffer less as you have less depression, less anxiety, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，通过冥想，你自己会因为抑郁、焦虑等的减少而减轻痛苦。

sentences.en: But it also is designed to awaken in people this sense of compassion and willing to help other individuals who are in need.
sentences.zh: 但它同时也旨在唤醒人们的慈悲心，以及帮助那些有需要的其他人的意愿。

sentences.en: And so, surprisingly, no one had ever looked at that.
sentences.zh: 所以，令人惊讶的是，以前从来没有人研究过这一点。

sentences.en: And so, we decided to take that seriously.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们决定认真对待它。

sentences.en: And so, we conducted a study where we brought people from the Boston area who had never meditated before but were interested in starting.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了一项研究，把波士顿地区从未冥想过但有兴趣开始尝试的人带到了实验室。

sentences.en: And we assigned them to either meditate for eight weeks where they had training with a
sentences.zh: 我们将他们分组，要么进行为期八周的冥想，接受

sentences.en: Buddhist lama or we put them on a wait liSt.
sentences.zh: 佛教喇嘛的指导，要么让他们进入等待名单。

sentences.en: So, two groups that were equally interested in meditation, none of them had meditated before.
sentences.zh: 所以，两组人对冥想的兴趣程度相同，且之前都没有冥想过。

sentences.en: One got treatment.
sentences.zh: 一组接受了治疗。

sentences.en: One got the intervention.
sentences.zh: 一组接受了干预。

sentences.en: One didn't.
sentences.zh: 另一组没有。

sentences.en: And at the end of those eight weeks, we'd bring them into our lab one at a time, telling them, we're going to give you some memory tests.
sentences.zh: 在八周结束时，我们一次一个人把他们带进实验室，告诉他们，我们要给你们做一些记忆测试。

sentences.en: That wasn't true.
sentences.zh: 那不是真的。

sentences.en: When they got to the lab, the real experiment took place in the waiting room.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达实验室时，真正的实验发生在候诊室里。

sentences.en: And in the waiting room, there were three chairs, two of which were occupied by actors that we hired, which our participants didn't know.
sentences.zh: 在候诊室里有三把椅子，其中两把坐着我们雇来的演员，参与者并不知道这一点。

sentences.en: When the participant came in, they'd, of course, take the third and last remaining chair.
sentences.zh: 当参与者进来时，他们当然会坐下最后剩下的第三把椅子。

sentences.en: About two minutes later, another actor came in and she was on crutches wearing one of those boots on her foot that you wear when your foot is broken.
sentences.zh: 大约两分钟后，另一位演员进来了，她拄着拐杖，脚上穿着那种脚骨折时穿的靴子。

sentences.en: It wasn't broken, but she would pretend she's in pain and wince and come in and there is no seats.
sentences.zh: 其实她的脚没断，但她会假装很痛苦，龇牙咧嘴地走进来，发现没有座位了。

sentences.en: And of course, the other actors were told to thumb their phones and ignore her.
sentences.zh: 当然，其他演员被告知要低头玩手机，无视她。

sentences.en: And the question was, what would the true research participants do?
sentences.zh: 问题是，真正的研究参与者会怎么做？

sentences.en: And what we found is that on average, only about 15% of the people who didn't meditate decided to get up and give them her chair.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，平均而言，只有约15%没有冥想过的人决定起身让座。

sentences.en: And you might say, well, that's pretty terrible.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But you see this on the subway or the bus all the time, right?
sentences.zh: 但你在地铁或公交车上经常看到这种情况，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: People just, they turn, oh, yeah, I don't give up my seat.
sentences.zh: 人们只是转过头，哦，是的，我不让座。

sentences.en: There's a mom with a toddler in tow or a person in pain.
sentences.zh: 旁边可能是一位带着幼儿的母亲，或者是一个痛苦的人。

sentences.en: But among the meditators, 50% did.
sentences.zh: 但在冥想者中，有50%的人让了座。

sentences.en: Now, that's a threefold difference, which is huge.
sentences.zh: 这是一个三倍的差距，非常巨大。

sentences.en: And we've replicated the study, so we know it's not a fluke.
sentences.zh: 我们已经重复了这项研究，所以我们知道这不是偶然。

sentences.en: And what this tells us is the Buddhist idea was right.
sentences.zh: 这告诉我们，佛教的理念是正确的。

sentences.en: Just engaging in this meditation practice after this, you know, eight weeks of time actually increased people's compassion.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是参与这种冥想练习，在八周的时间后，确实增加了人们的慈悲心。

sentences.en: We've done subsequent studies where we have, through long shenanigans I'm not going to bore you with, we have people actually get insulted by actors in a way that usually makes
sentences.zh: 我们还做了后续研究，通过一些我不打算用琐事来烦你的手段，让人们被演员以一种通常会让人

sentences.en: them pretty angry.
sentences.zh: 感到非常愤怒的方式侮辱。

sentences.en: And then we give them a way that they think they can seek vengeance on this person.
sentences.zh: 然后我们给他们提供一种他们认为可以向此人报复的方式。

sentences.en: Of course, they can't really do it, but they think they can.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们并不能真的报复，但他们以为可以。

sentences.en: And what we find is that, you know, after so many weeks of meditation, people reduce the vengeance they want to take on this person who insulted them.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，经过几周的冥想后，人们减少了对侮辱他们的人进行报复的念头。

sentences.en: They don't rise with aggression to provocation.
sentences.zh: 他们不会因为挑衅而产生攻击性。

sentences.en: And so what this tells us is that, you know, there is some truth here.
sentences.zh: 所以这告诉我们，这里面确实有一些真理。

sentences.en: Um, and you know, another thing we work on in my lab is this notion of, of, of what gratitude does.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我在实验室里研究的另一件事是关于感恩的作用。

sentences.en: And we found time and again that when people feel grateful by expressing their gratitude to God for what they have, to friends, family, to fate, whatever it might be, we find that
sentences.zh: 我们一次又一次地发现，当人们通过向神、向朋友、家人、命运或任何事物表达感恩来感受感激时，我们发现

sentences.en: it makes them more generous.
sentences.zh: 这会使他们变得更慷慨。

sentences.en: It makes them more patient.
sentences.zh: 这会使他们变得更有耐心。

sentences.en: It makes them, um, uh, more willing to share what they have and trust other people and not just the people to whom they're grateful, anybody.
sentences.zh: 这会使他们更愿意分享自己拥有的东西，更愿意信任他人，不仅仅是对那些他们感恩的人，而是对任何人。

sentences.en: And if you look at religions, right, every religion has ways to foster gratitude.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看宗教，对吧，每个宗教都有培养感恩的方式。

sentences.en: Christians say, uh, prayers of grace.
sentences.zh: 基督徒会做感恩祷告。

sentences.en: When they eat Jews every day, when the morning they get up, they say the moda ani prayer, which
sentences.zh: 犹太人每天吃饭时，早上起床时，会念“Moda Ani”祷告，这

sentences.en: is a thank you to God for, you know, returning me to this earth for another day, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 是对上帝的感谢，感谢他让我重回人间又过了一天，等等。

sentences.en: And so the, the interesting thing about religion is any behavioral scientist will tell you, we all have intentions.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于宗教有趣的一点是，任何行为科学家都会告诉你，我们都有意图。

sentences.en: We all have things that we want to do, like in this case, be a better person, but unless we have strategies or tools, we don't get there.
sentences.zh: 我们都有想做的事情，比如在这种情况下，成为一个更好的人，但除非我们有策略或工具，否则我们无法实现。

sentences.en: Think about new year's resolutions, right?
sentences.zh: 想想新年决心，对吧？

sentences.en: By mid January, 25% have failed by the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 到一月中旬，25%的人已经失败了，到年底时。

sentences.en: Only 8% have been kept all the way through.
sentences.zh: 只有8%的人坚持到底。

sentences.en: We need tools to, to help us reach our goals.
sentences.zh: 我们需要工具来帮助我们实现目标。

sentences.en: And what religions are doing in these rituals is not just telling us how we should be, but giving us the tools to make it more likely that we can be that way.
sentences.zh: 而宗教在这些仪式中所做的，不仅仅是告诉我们应该成为什么样的人，而是给了我们工具，让我们更有可能成为那样的人。

sentences.en: So meditation sounds kind of magical and you have talked about finding the next meditation.
sentences.zh: 所以冥想听起来有点神奇，你还谈到了寻找“下一个冥想”。

sentences.en: Um, why, why do, if meditation itself is so great, why do we need the next next meditation?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么，如果冥想本身已经这么棒了，为什么我们需要下一个冥想？

sentences.en: What are we looking for?
sentences.zh: 我们在寻找什么？

sentences.en: What do you mean when you say that?
sentences.zh: 当你这么说时，你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean by that, so meditation is a wonderful tool for becoming kinder, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，冥想是一个让人变得更友善的绝佳工具，对吧？

sentences.en: Becoming more compassionate, but there's other things that we want to do in life, right?
sentences.zh: 变得更有同情心，但生活中还有其他我们想做的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: How do I, how do I become happier?
sentences.zh: 我该如何变得更快乐？

sentences.en: Um, and so yes, meditation will reduce anxiety, depression, but how does it find, does it help you find meaning in life?
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以是的，冥想会减少焦虑和抑郁，但它能帮你找到人生的意义吗？

sentences.en: Not exactly.
sentences.zh: 不完全是。

sentences.en: So another thing that people do, you know, if you look at happiness across the lifespan,
sentences.zh: 所以人们做的另一件事，你知道，如果你观察整个生命周期的幸福感，

sentences.en: it tends to, uh, drop at its, hit its nadir around 40 and 50 and then begins to go up.
sentences.zh: 它往往会在40到50岁左右降至最低点，然后开始上升。

sentences.en: And there's, there's wonderful evidence from psychologist, Laura Karstensen that shows that as people age, they turn their, uh, desires from kind of wanting to get ahead in life,
sentences.zh: 心理学家劳拉·卡斯滕森（Laura Carstensen）有极好的证据表明，随着人们年龄增长，他们会将欲望从想要在生活中出人头地、

sentences.en: building skills, you know, building status to focus on friends, family, and, and service things that actually have been shown to bring more happiness in life.
sentences.zh: 建立技能、建立地位，转向关注朋友、家人和服务，这些事情已被证明能带来更多的生活幸福感。

sentences.en: But although it looks like it's a function of age, what her work has really shown is that
sentences.zh: 但尽管这看起来像是年龄的函数，她的研究真正表明的是，

sentences.en: it's a function of what she calls a time horizon, which is how long I have left until I die.
sentences.zh: 这是她所说的“时间跨度”的函数，也就是我离死亡还有多久。

sentences.en: And so what you see, uh, in her work and work of other folks is that during pandemics, like
sentences.zh: 所以你在她的研究和其他人的研究中看到的是，在大流行期间，就像

sentences.en: we've all been facing now, that age difference goes away because suddenly even young people,
sentences.zh: 我们现在都面临的那样，这种年龄差异消失了，因为突然间，即使是年轻人，

sentences.en: even people in their twenties and thirties are thinking, I may not have as much time left.
sentences.zh: 甚至是二三十岁的人也在想，我剩下的时间可能不多了。

sentences.en: Uh, and suddenly they look like they're seniors.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们看起来就像老年人一样。

sentences.en: They are valuing friends, family, uh, finding meaning through service in life.
sentences.zh: 他们开始重视朋友、家人，通过服务他人来寻找人生的意义。

sentences.en: Um, but we don't want to face a pandemic to have to make this kind of correction to find a new way to find happiness.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我们不想面对一场大流行才被迫做出这种修正，去寻找一种寻找幸福的新方式。

sentences.en: And so what you see in religious rituals is, is before periods of taking stock.
sentences.zh: 所以你在宗教仪式中看到的是，在这些时期之前进行盘点。

sentences.en: So if, if you're a Jew during, uh, the days of all before Yom Kippur is a time to take stock of, of your life.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是犹太人，在赎罪日之前的敬畏之日，是盘点你人生的时间。

sentences.en: If you're a Christian, it's during the period of Lent, a time to take stock of, of yourself before each of those, uh, there's for Christians, there's Ash
sentences.zh: 如果你是基督徒，是在大斋期，在每个时期之前盘点你自己，对于基督徒来说，有圣灰

sentences.en: Wednesday, which is a reminder of your own mortality, right?
sentences.zh: 星期三，这是对你自身必死性的提醒，对吧？

sentences.en: The priest actually puts ashes on your head and says from dust, you came and onto dust, you shall return.
sentences.zh: 牧师会在你的额头上涂上灰烬，说你来自尘土，终将归于尘土。

sentences.en: Um, on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, uh, Jews say a prayer called the Moda Ani, which, uh, has in it a part that says who is going to live
sentences.zh: 嗯，在犹太新年和赎罪日，犹太人会念一段叫“Moda Ani”的祷告，其中有一部分说谁将在未来一年

sentences.en: and who's going to die in their coming year before their time, who by fire, who by sword, who by flood, who by plague this year, that one kind of hit really hard.
sentences.zh: 生，谁将死，谁在命定之前，谁死于火，谁死于剑，谁死于洪水，谁死于瘟疫，这一年，那一段真的让人感触很深。

sentences.en: And again, it's a reminder that your time here, it may not be as long as you think.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是在提醒你，你在这里的时间，可能没有你想象的那么长。

sentences.en: And what that does is it begins to shift your values.
sentences.zh: 而这所做的，是开始转变你的价值观。

sentences.en: Like even, even Laura Carstensen showed that if you make older people say, she said,
sentences.zh: 就像劳拉·卡斯滕森展示的那样，如果你让老年人说，她说，

sentences.en: imagine that you're going to live a lot longer than you thought, because there's this new medicine
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你会比你想象的活得更久，因为有一种新药

sentences.en: that will help you live a healthier life for 20 or 30 years more than you expected.
sentences.zh: 能帮助你比预期多活20到30年的健康生活。

sentences.en: Suddenly they start focusing on skills and their idiosyncratic desires as they look like younger people.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们开始像年轻人一样关注技能和他们特有的欲望。

sentences.en: So just these little nudges can matter.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅是这些小小的推动就能产生影响。

sentences.en: And what you're seeing in these rituals is a way to help us focus at times that we should be taking stock of our lives on what really matters in ways to bring happiness.
sentences.zh: 你在这些仪式中看到的是一种帮助我们在应该盘点人生时，专注于真正重要的事情，从而带来幸福的方法。

sentences.en: And it's why both Jewish scholars, Christian scholars, Muslim scholars have said, you know, it's, it's don't wait for just once a year either, you know, every day, think about
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么犹太学者、基督教学者、穆斯林学者都说，你知道，不要只等一年一次，每天都要思考

sentences.en: what am I doing?
sentences.zh: 我在做什么？

sentences.en: And is, you know, is this what I'd want to do if I weren't going to see tomorrow?
sentences.zh: 如果我明天看不到了，这还是我想做的事吗？

sentences.en: So there's lots of examples like that.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多这样的例子。

sentences.en: There's lots of other ways, you know, people now are getting very into taking psychedelics for transcendent experiences.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他方式，你知道，人们现在非常热衷于服用迷幻剂来获得超验体验。

sentences.en: But what they're not adopting is also the rituals that typically surrounded those transcending, those use of psychedelics, which put
sentences.zh: 但他们没有采用的，是通常围绕着那些超验体验、那些迷幻剂使用的仪式，这些仪式让

sentences.en: people in a physiological state of calmness and connectedness so that when that moment of ego death came, it would be pleasurable and not terrifying.
sentences.zh: 人们处于一种平静和连接的生理状态，这样当“自我死亡”的时刻到来时，它会是愉悦的，而不是可怕的。

sentences.en: Because right now, you know, 10, 20% of the time, people have these experiences on psychedelics, and they're frightening, they're not wonderful.
sentences.zh: 因为现在，你知道，10%到20%的情况下，人们在服用迷幻剂时会有这些体验，而且它们是令人恐惧的，而不是美妙的。

sentences.en: And 8% of the time they actually seek psychiatric care after.
sentences.zh: 而且8%的情况下，他们事后确实寻求了精神科护理。

sentences.en: And it's because as Michael Pollan has said, if you're not in the right state of mind, when that moment comes, the experience can go very badly.
sentences.zh: 这是因为正如迈克尔·波伦（Michael Pollan）所说，如果你在那个时刻没有处于正确的心理状态，体验可能会变得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And what these rituals do is they make sure you're in that frame of mind.
sentences.zh: 而这些仪式的作用就是确保你处于那种心态中。

sentences.en: So while we're taking the psychoactive chemicals and giving them to people by ignoring the rituals that put that body and mind in the right
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们摄入精神活性化学物质并将其给予人们时，却忽视了那些让身体和心灵处于正确状态的仪式。

sentences.en: frame, we're, you know, increasing the odds that things aren't going to go as well as they should.
sentences.zh: 框架，我们，你知道，正在增加事情不会像预期的那样顺利进行的几率。

sentences.en: But now that doesn't have to be a religious preparation, right?
sentences.zh: 但现在这不一定非得是某种宗教准备，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, there are psychologists who are doing this work right now with psychedelics, and they will also sort of walk people through,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在有一些心理学家正在用迷幻药做这项工作，他们也会引导人们，

sentences.en: prepare them so that when you take the psychedelic, you won't have, as you're describing, a bad trip.
sentences.zh: 为他们做好准备，这样当你服用迷幻药时，就不会像你描述的那样，经历一次糟糕的旅程。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if you look at some of the best research coming out right now is coming from
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看看目前一些最好的研究，它们来自

sentences.en: Johns Hopkins, Roland Griffith's lab.
sentences.zh: 约翰霍普金斯大学，罗兰·格里菲斯的实验室。

sentences.en: And I've talked to people there.
sentences.zh: 我和那里的人谈过。

sentences.en: And what's basically happening is you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 基本上发生的情况是，你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: The researcher spends time with you, they build that sense of trust and rapport beforehand, they sit with you during it.
sentences.zh: 研究人员会花时间和你在一起，他们会提前建立那种信任和融洽的关系，并在过程中陪伴着你。

sentences.en: And if you start to have a bad reaction, they'll hold your hand, they'll put their hand on your cheSt. And afterward, they will help you make sense of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你开始有不良反应，他们会握住你的手，把手放在你的胸口。事后，他们会帮你理清这一切。

sentences.en: In essence, they're doing exactly what a shaman would do without the religious symbology around it.
sentences.zh: 本质上，他们做的正是萨满会做的事情，只是去掉了周围的宗教象征意义。

sentences.en: But because they're putting you in that state of calm, trusting feeling with them, that's the scaffold that is there to help make sure that the experience goes the right way.
sentences.zh: 但因为他们让你处于那种平静、信任他们的状态，这就是帮助确保体验朝着正确方向发展的支架。

sentences.en: Whereas with a shaman, you would do that, and he or she would help guide you.
sentences.zh: 而在萨满那里，你会这样做，他或她会帮助引导你。

sentences.en: But they also sing these chants together and use these drumming rhythms that, again, change people's breathing
sentences.zh: 但他们也会一起唱这些圣歌，并使用这些鼓点节奏，这同样会改变人们的呼吸

sentences.en: and respiration rates, make them feel calm, make them feel connected again before it happens.
sentences.zh: 和呼吸频率，让他们感到平静，在事情发生前让他们再次感到连接。

sentences.en: So you're right, you don't need the religious symbology.
sentences.zh: 所以你是对的，你不需要宗教象征意义。

sentences.en: And that's the point I'm trying to make here, which is, when I talk about this, people say, well, Dave, are you, you know, isn't that cultural appropriation what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 这就是我试图表达的观点，当我谈论这个时，人们会说，嗯，戴夫，你，你知道，你所说的不就是文化挪用吗？

sentences.en: Or if I'm a Christian, why do I want to take a Jewish ritual or a Hindu ritual?
sentences.zh: 或者如果我是基督徒，我为什么要采用犹太教或印度教的仪式？

sentences.en: And I'm not in favor of cultural appropriation, I would never want to take these rituals and take the actual prayers and the symbols and the theological meaning from them,
sentences.zh: 我并不支持文化挪用，我永远不想采用这些仪式，并从中拿走实际的祈祷文、符号和神学意义，

sentences.en: because those belong to the faith that originated them and should be respected.
sentences.zh: 因为那些属于起源于它们的信仰，应该受到尊重。

sentences.en: But there are elements of them that can be taken in the breathing people use, in the way they interact
sentences.zh: 但其中有一些元素是可以借鉴的，比如人们使用的呼吸方式，他们互动的方式，

sentences.en: together, in the way they sing, in the way physiologically that they interact during prayer that can be taken and used in a secular context.
sentences.zh: 他们唱歌的方式，以及他们在祈祷时生理上互动的方式，这些都可以被借鉴并用于世俗环境中。

sentences.en: And, you know, don't just take it from me, those don't belong to any one religion.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，别只听我的一面之词，这些并不属于任何单一的宗教。

sentences.en: You see a lot of those things used in multiple religions, just with different vocabularies and different theologies and different symbologies.
sentences.zh: 你会看到很多这样的东西被用于多种宗教中，只是有着不同的词汇、不同的神学和不同的象征意义。

sentences.en: And so my argument is, let's learn what they're doing to the body and mind in a secular sense.
sentences.zh: 所以我的论点是，让我们从世俗的角度去了解它们对身心有什么影响。

sentences.en: Put that under the scientific microscope, see when it matters and how we can use that to help people, while respecting,
sentences.zh: 把这些放在科学的显微镜下，看看它们在什么时候起作用，以及我们如何利用它们来帮助人们，同时尊重，

sentences.en: you know, the cultural symbols and theologies of the religions themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，宗教本身的文化符号和神学。

sentences.en: So we've been talking a lot about how religion can make people happier and provide comfort.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直在讨论宗教如何能让人更快乐并提供慰藉。

sentences.en: But, you know, there's another side of religion as well, which is the threat of punishment, of eternal damnation.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，宗教还有另一面，那就是惩罚的威胁，永恒的诅咒。

sentences.en: Is that something that you have looked at and is threatening people in that way effective in making them behave ethically?
sentences.zh: 这是你研究过的课题吗？以这种方式威胁人们在促使他们遵守道德行为方面有效吗？

sentences.en: What's happening in your brain when you're being threatened by your religion?
sentences.zh: 当你受到宗教威胁时，你的大脑里发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, two things there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有两点。

sentences.en: One, religions can cause guilt and cause shame.
sentences.zh: 第一，宗教会导致内疚和羞耻感。

sentences.en: And as a psychologist who studies social behavior, I can tell you guilt and shame are extremely motivating and can be very
sentences.zh: 作为一名研究社会行为的心理学家，我可以告诉你，内疚和羞耻感是非常强大的动力，在短时间内可能非常

sentences.en: effective in small, brief doses, but used over the long haul are not helpful and cause a lot of pain.
sentences.zh: 有效，但长期使用则无益，且会造成很多痛苦。

sentences.en: And so, again, you know, what I tell people is I'm not an apologist for religion.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次强调，你知道，我告诉人们我不是宗教的辩护者。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: Steve Pinker and I always get into arguments about this.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·平克和我总是为此争论不休。

sentences.en: And he says, Dave, you're cherry picking.
sentences.zh: 他说，戴夫，你在挑拣证据。

sentences.en: There's lots of religion about religion that's bad, right?
sentences.zh: 关于宗教有很多糟糕的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: It causes people guilt and shame.
sentences.zh: 它导致人们产生内疚和羞耻感。

sentences.en: It's perpetuated discrimination.
sentences.zh: 它延续了歧视。

sentences.en: It's caused war and strife.
sentences.zh: 它导致了战争和冲突。

sentences.en: And I'm like, Steve, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我说，史蒂夫，你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: But I am cherry picking because I want to know what works and what's helpful.
sentences.zh: 但我确实是在挑拣，因为我想知道什么有效，什么有帮助。

sentences.en: I'm not here to defend religion.
sentences.zh: 我不是来为宗教辩护的。

sentences.en: And so my argument is if you look at these practices, religion, so take the theology out for a moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我的论点是，如果你看看这些实践，宗教，暂时抛开神学不谈。

sentences.en: The tools that religion has developed are powerful tools to motivate us to shape what we feel and do.
sentences.zh: 宗教所发展的工具是强大的工具，可以激励我们塑造我们的感受和行为。

sentences.en: They can be used for good or for ill.
sentences.zh: 它们可以被用于善，也可以被用于恶。

sentences.en: It all depends upon the intentions of the people using it, just like science, right?
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于使用它们的人的意图，就像科学一样，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Richard Dawkins has said, if you want to find the most efficient way to kill the most people possible, science is your friend.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，理查德·道金斯曾说，如果你想找到杀死最多人的最有效方法，科学是你的朋友。

sentences.en: He's right.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。

sentences.en: If you want to find the way to save people from COVID, science is your friend.
sentences.zh: 如果你想找到拯救人们免受新冠病毒侵害的方法，科学是你的朋友。

sentences.en: He's right.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。

sentences.en: I think about religion the same way in the sense that the tools of spiritual practices, I tend to separate from the
sentences.zh: 我以同样的方式看待宗教，即精神实践的工具，我倾向于将它们与

sentences.en: institutions and the purposes and goals that those institutions have.
sentences.zh: 这些机构所拥有的制度、目的和目标分离开来。

sentences.en: So yes, religion has caused people lots of pain and caused them to deny science even.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，宗教给人们带来了很多痛苦，甚至导致他们否认科学。

sentences.en: But you see that now even with political ideologies, right?
sentences.zh: 但你现在即使在政治意识形态中也能看到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: We're seeing as a function of political ideology, people deny science when it comes to vaccines and COVID.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，作为政治意识形态的一种功能，人们在疫苗和新冠病毒问题上否认科学。

sentences.en: And so I don't think that's a problem so much of religion as a much of ideological institutions.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这与其说是宗教的问题，不如说是意识形态机构的问题。

sentences.en: But even if that's what you believe, then it's still worthwhile studying how these tools work so that you can prevent and remediate the problematic aspects of them.
sentences.zh: 但即使那是你的信仰，研究这些工具如何运作仍然是值得的，这样你就可以预防和纠正它们的问题方面。

sentences.en: Last topic that I want to cover here.
sentences.zh: 我想在这里讨论的最后一个话题。

sentences.en: I talked a little bit about how religious or irreligious
sentences.zh: 我谈到了一些关于宗教或非宗教

sentences.en: Americans are these days.
sentences.zh: 美国人如今的情况。

sentences.en: A 2021 Gallup poll found that for the first time since they started polling in the 1940s, less than half of Americans said they belonged to a church, a synagogue, or a mosque.
sentences.zh: 2021年盖洛普的一项民意调查发现，自20世纪40年代开始民意调查以来，首次有不到一半的美国人表示他们属于某个教堂、犹太教堂或清真寺。

sentences.en: So given your research, what do you think the effects of that will be?
sentences.zh: 那么根据你的研究，你认为这会产生什么影响？

sentences.en: Will people be less happy because they're not engaged in religion or less moral?
sentences.zh: 人们会因为不参与宗教而变得不那么快乐或不那么有道德吗？

sentences.en: Or are they replacing religion with something else?
sentences.zh: 还是他们正在用其他东西取代宗教？

sentences.en: So it is true, as you said, that people are leaving traditional faith in droves.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，人们确实正在成群结队地离开传统信仰，这是事实。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing is when you look more closely at those data, most of them aren't becoming atheists, right?
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，当你更仔细地观察这些数据时，他们中的大多数人并没有变成无神论者，对吧？

sentences.en: Most of them are calling themselves nuns, N-O-N-E-S, which is none of the above, right?
sentences.zh: 他们中的大多数人称自己为“无宗教信仰者”（Nones），也就是以上皆非，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm not Christian, I'm not Jewish, I'm not Hindu, I'm not Muslim.
sentences.zh: 我不是基督徒，不是犹太教徒，不是印度教徒，也不是穆斯林。

sentences.en: But they're looking for new ways to be spiritual.
sentences.zh: 但他们正在寻找新的方式来获得精神寄托。

sentences.en: And I think it's because they, in leaving these institutions, that in some ways there are good reasons to leave for people, they've failed them.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为他们在离开这些机构时，在某些方面人们离开是有正当理由的，它们辜负了他们。

sentences.en: There have been, you know, financial scandals, abuse scandals, gender discrimination, even sometimes you don't just believe the theology.
sentences.zh: 你知道，曾经有过金融丑闻、虐待丑闻、性别歧视，甚至有时你只是不相信那种神学。

sentences.en: People recognize that they're leaving behind that sense of community and those tools that help them find meaning and meet the challenges of life.
sentences.zh: 人们意识到他们正在抛弃那种社区感以及那些帮助他们寻找意义和应对生活挑战的工具。

sentences.en: And so I think right now we're going through a time period of people are looking for another way.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为现在我们正经历一个人们正在寻找另一种方式的时期。

sentences.en: Now, you know, when Nietzsche said
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道，当尼采说

sentences.en: God is dead and we have killed him and, you know, the world's going to fall into chaos, he wasn't right.
sentences.zh: 上帝死了，我们杀了他，你知道，世界将陷入混乱，他并不正确。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, we become much more secular.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我们变得更加世俗化了。

sentences.en: The world isn't full of chaos.
sentences.zh: 世界并没有充满混乱。

sentences.en: You can certainly be a good person without religion.
sentences.zh: 你当然可以在没有宗教的情况下成为一个好人。

sentences.en: But I do think it fills psychological needs and helps us meet the challenges of life.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为它满足了心理需求，并帮助我们应对生活的挑战。

sentences.en: It's not just the opiate of the masses, it's actually a cultural tool that we've developed to help us meet challenges.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是大众的鸦片，它实际上是我们为了帮助自己应对挑战而发展出来的一种文化工具。

sentences.en: And so I do worry a bit that you're going to see declines in well-being that track this leaving of spirituality unless people do find new ways.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实有点担心，除非人们找到新的方式，否则你会看到幸福感的下降，这与这种离开精神信仰的趋势相吻合。

sentences.en: And to me, that's why I think science needs to take this seriously.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是为什么我认为科学需要认真对待这一点。

sentences.en: If you look at that data, in a dose-response framework, people who are more engaged with spiritual practices live longer, healthier, and happier lives.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看那些数据，在剂量反应框架下，更多参与精神实践的人生活得更长寿、更健康、更快乐。

sentences.en: That means, as psychologists, it's our job to figure out why, what are those practices doing, and if people are giving them up, how can we find ways to replace them?
sentences.zh: 这意味着，作为心理学家，我们的工作是找出原因，这些实践在做什么，如果人们放弃了它们，我们如何找到方法来取代它们？

sentences.en: And thus the search for the next meditation.
sentences.zh: 因此，寻找下一种冥想方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。
